method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023' (published 16 April 2024), 22 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at licence statement printed on page 1 of the article PDF). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150) 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice' (published 18 January 2025), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12206285). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps the APAC APCCC 2023 claims (S1) unchanged and adds Australian practical guidance on BRCA testing in mCRPC (S2, PMC12206285): Medicare-funded test pathways, tissue handling, germline testing and consent, ctDNA, and olaparib access. S2 is a narrative practical-guidance review; its medical writing was funded by AstraZeneca (which markets olaparib).

claims.claim: **Next-generation imaging (PSMA PET-CT, whole-body MRI) stages prostate cancer more accurately than conventional imaging**, and PSMA PET-CT has the strongest evidence, with less radiation and less reader variability.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PSMA PET-CT can give false positives**, so an experienced nuclear medicine physician should read it. Do not withhold beneficial treatment of the primary tumour just because PSMA PET shows small lymph nodes.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Order a test only if its result will change the management plan.**
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Disease volume on conventional imaging (CHAARTED definition) shapes treatment, especially whether to use docetaxel** (85% of panelists). Whether metastases were present at diagnosis or appeared later also changes sequencing, metastasis-directed therapy, triplet choice and prostate radiotherapy (69%).
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intensify beyond ADT alone.** For high-volume disease 84% would combine ADT with an androgen receptor signalling inhibitor (ARSi) and/or docetaxel; for low-volume disease 69% would use a combination and only 15% ADT alone.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ADT alone is sub-optimal when an ARSi can be given**; the minority (15%) who use it for low-volume disease do so because of reimbursement rules.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Triplet therapy (ADT + ARSi + docetaxel) may not add survival over an ARSi doublet**, according to a meta-analysis of five trials. Because toxicity accumulates, reserve triplets for chemo-fit patients with high-volume, poor-prognosis disease.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If a patient is doing well on a doublet, adding docetaxel is hard to justify**; for some with the worst prognostic features, ADT may suffice and de-escalation may help.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low-volume synchronous mHSPC: add radiotherapy to the prostate** (88% of panelists), and consider metastasis-directed therapy for selected patients (85%).
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cost workarounds are common in the region:** about half (54%) give lower-dose abiraterone with food, a practice changing with the 500 mg tablet. Fear of chemotherapy also limits docetaxel use in some Asian populations.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PSA doubling time matters more than imaging for prognosis in nmCRPC.** Baseline PSA and doubling time predict metastasis and survival; RADAR III reserves next-generation imaging for doubling time under 6 months when M1 treatment would be appropriate.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider an ARSi when PSA doubling time is under 10 months** and there has been no local therapy (54%). With doubling time over 10 months, opinion splits between observation, prostate radiotherapy, or local therapy plus ARSi.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On an ARSi, most (58%) monitor PSA alone**, though the trials used imaging as well and progression can happen without a PSA rise.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Up to 23% of men with mCRPC carry actionable mutations.** BRCA is commonest (about half germline); ATM is also frequent but responds less well to treatment.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Plan testing as the disease approaches castration resistance**, since PARP inhibitors such as olaparib benefit BRCA-mutated cancers. At minimum take a family history; refer for specialist genetic counselling before germline testing or when somatic testing finds a pathogenic HRR mutation.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tissue can limit testing:** archived primary biopsies often have small samples and poor DNA yield or quality; alternatives include biopsy of other sites, ctDNA and germline testing.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BRCA2 is the commonest target:** about 3.9% of men with mCRPC carry a germline and 10.5% a somatic BRCA2 mutation, against 1.2% and 1.1% for BRCA1. BRCA-mutant cells cannot repair the DNA damage PARP inhibitors cause.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Medicare funds BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing after an mCRPC diagnosis to decide PARP-inhibitor eligibility:** tumour testing with follow-on germline characterisation if that is inconclusive (MBS item 73303), germline testing when tumour testing is not feasible (item 73304), and germline confirmation after a positive tumour result (item 73302). Only NATA-accredited laboratories using validated tests can claim.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tumour tissue NGS is the gold standard** and finds both somatic and germline variants, though it cannot reliably say which (especially at allele fractions around 30% or more), so confirm with germline testing. Start early enough that a BRCA-positive patient is not kept waiting for olaparib.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Do germline testing when tumour tissue shows a pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant, or when family history or ancestry suggests it, after informed consent** (an Australian Genomics national consent form exists). Oncologists increasingly consent patients themselves ('mainstream' testing), but still refer to a familial cancer clinic to verify tissue findings in the germline, for cascade testing of relatives, and for a worrying family history even when tissue testing is negative.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tumour testing often fails: 31% of 4047 PROfound patients had no result.** Archived blocks gave results in 68% when under 1 year old, 62% at 1–3 years and 47% beyond 10 years, so use samples under 3 years old where possible; if FFPE testing fails, test germline blood or use a liquid biopsy.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Handle new biopsies for later sequencing:** put tissue in formalin within 1 h to avoid cold ischaemia, fix in 10% neutral buffered formalin for 8–24 h (cores) or no more than 48 h (resections), avoid over-fixation, and ask for EDTA (not acid) decalcification of bone biopsies. Most NGS platforms need at least 10% or 20% tumour cellularity.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **On the request form, give the diagnosis and original pathology report, say the specimen is for molecular testing and which gene, and flag urgency.** Comprehensive panels can take weeks, so retrieve and send blocks promptly.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **ctDNA agrees reasonably with tissue (81% positive, 92% negative agreement for BRCA1/2 and ATM)** and can complement it when tissue is inadequate, but it is not routine or Medicare-reimbursed in Australia for mCRPC.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **First-line mCRPC without a DNA-repair mutation depends on what was used for mHSPC:** after ADT alone (65%) or ADT + docetaxel (77%), an ARSi; after ADT + ARSi, docetaxel (73%); after ADT + ARSi + docetaxel, Lu-177 PSMA (50%).
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not switch from one ARSi to another on progression without an actionable mutation** (the international consensus); it offers little and adds cost and toxicity, though 27% of regional panelists still switch for cost or patient preference.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BRCA-mutated mCRPC:** half the panel (50%) uses a PARP inhibitor alone; ARSi-plus-PARPi combinations are approved first line in some countries.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Docetaxel can be re-tried in mCRPC** after a reasonable gap since its use for mHSPC (62%). Cabazitaxel is an option, but worries about chemotherapy and bone-marrow suppression lead some to prefer Lu-177 PSMA where it is available.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor mCRPC clinically and with PSA**; the usual view is to image only when PSA or symptoms suggest progression.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Olaparib in Australia:** PBS-subsidised for mCRPC with a pathogenic or likely pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation that has progressed after an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (PROfound: median survival 19.1 vs 14.7 months against a switch of ARPI, HR 0.69). Olaparib with abiraterone and prednisone or prednisolone is also TGA-approved for BRCA-mutated mCRPC.
claims.locator: Azad A, Gurney H, Campbell A, Goh JC, Rathi V, Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 21(4):345 (doi 10.1111/ajco.14150), 'BRCA Mutation Testing in Men With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Practical Guidance for Australian Clinical Practice', published 18 January 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12206285/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Use geriatric assessment for older men** (77% recommend it), in practice usually when red-flag issues come up. Supportive care includes bone protection, screening for and preventing metabolic syndrome, and exercise physiology.
claims.locator: Chiong E, Murphy DG, ... Davis ID, for ANZUP Cancer Trials Group (APAC APCCC 2023), Asia-Pacific Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;20:481-490, 'Management of advanced prostate cancer in the Asia-Pacific region: Summary of the Asia-Pacific Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference 2023', published 16 April 2024, https://anzup.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Chiong-et-al-APAC-APCCC-APJCO-2024.pdf (DOI 10.1111/ajco.14064), retrieved 2026-09-23
